request: Build a mobile-friendly landing page for $500. The contact form must work, the website must be accessible and Lighthouse performance must score at least 90.

A working contact form on the landing page
A landing page that meets the buyer's accessibility expectation

ambiguities.question: Should the Lighthouse performance score of at least 90 be measured on mobile, on desktop, or on both?
What exactly do you mean by 'accessible' — is there a standard and level you want met (for example a specific WCAG version and level), and who decides whether it is met?
What counts as the contact form 'working' — a visible success confirmation after submitting, an email arriving at a specific address, or both? If email delivery matters, which address?
At which URL (and on whose hosting/domain) will the finished landing page be delivered for verification?
Is the deliverable a single landing page only, or does 'the website must be accessible' refer to additional pages as well?

manual_review_items.reason: Accessibility is not covered by any automated criterion kind and the buyer did not state a standard, so a human must review it against a definition the buyer confirms.

grounded.summary: The run completed with an overall verdict of fail. Three blocking checks passed: the landing page returned HTTP 200 on the first request with no redirects, the page fit a 390px-wide mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow, and Lighthouse mobile performance scored 100 against a minimum of 90. The blocking contact-form check failed: the form and all three expected fields were found and filled, but after clicking the submit button no request reached the test sink, no receipt was recorded, and the expected 'Thank you' confirmation never appeared. One non-blocking accessibility criterion is flagged for manual review because the buyer did not define an accessibility standard; no automated measurement was taken for it.

explanations.explanation: A request to the landing page path '/' resolved in a single hop to http://127.0.0.1:8020/landing-page-broken/ with status 200 and no redirect location, completing in 61 ms, which satisfies the expected status of 200 within the 10000 ms timeout and 5-redirect limit. The HTTP trace artifact records this chain.

Rendered at a 390x844 viewport, the page returned HTTP 200 and its scroll width equalled the viewport width (390 = 390), so there was no horizontal overflow as required. No required visible selectors were specified, so the selectors_visible map is empty. The mobile screenshot artifact documents the rendered page.

The checker found the form ('form_found' true) and none of the three expected fields were missing, so name, email and message were filled as specified. After clicking button[type=submit], however, 'sink_requests' is an empty list and 'sink_receipts_in_db' is 0, meaning no submission ever reached the configured test endpoint, and 'success_text_seen' is false, meaning the expected 'Thank you' confirmation never rendered. The reason code is NO_SUBMISSION_TO_SINK. No prohibited or unrelated blocked requests were recorded, so the failure is not attributable to egress filtering in this evidence. The post-submit screenshot shows the page state after the click. The measurements do not reveal the underlying cause (for example a missing form action, a JavaScript error, or a disabled submit handler).
explanations.remediation: Make the contact form actually submit to the agreed test endpoint: give the <form> a real action/method (or an onsubmit/fetch handler) pointing at the configured 'default' test endpoint, and ensure the button[type=submit] is inside the form, not disabled, and that its default action is not cancelled by preventDefault() without a replacement network call. Verify in the browser devtools Network tab that clicking submit issues a POST carrying the name, email and message values, and that the page then renders visible text containing the exact string 'Thank you' (not only inside a hidden element, an alert, or a redirect that is blocked). Re-test at a 390px viewport with JavaScript console open to catch any script error that aborts submission.

explanations.explanation: A single Lighthouse mobile run with simulated throttling scored 100 against the required minimum of 90, placing the result in band 5 with no adaptive retry needed. The run took 10016 ms and the full report is stored as the Lighthouse JSON artifact.

missing_evidence: Browser console/JavaScript error log from the contact-form run, which would show whether a script error prevented submission
The DOM/HTML of the form element (action, method, handler attributes) at the time of the check

A network log scoped to the contact-form interaction showing any outbound request attempts after the submit click; the run includes an egress-decisions network log artifact (2c0769ea-dfd1-4a0e-82e2-9fe9f0dfe6d5) but it is not linked to any result
A pre-submit screenshot to confirm the fields were visibly populated before the click
An agreed accessibility standard and any automated accessibility scan output for the website_accessible criterion
limitations: Verdicts were produced by deterministic tooling; this explanation reports them and cannot change them, and it carries no authority over payment.
The contact-form evidence shows the absence of a submission but not its cause, so the remediation lists plausible fixes rather than a confirmed root cause.
Checks were run against a local host (http://127.0.0.1:8020/landing-page-broken/), so behaviour on the production domain or over HTTPS was not verified (require_https was false).
Lighthouse performance is based on a single simulated mobile run and may vary across runs and real devices.
Artifacts were referenced by id and hash only; their contents were not independently re-examined here.
